source.title: 1-bit LAMB: Communication Efficient Large-Scale Large-Batch Training with LAMB’s Convergence Speed
source.authors: Cong-Long Li; A. Awan; Hanlin Tang; Samyam Rajbhandari; Yuxiong He

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that freezing LAMB’s variance and scaling coefficient during compression slows convergence and reduces downstream scores, while its revised 1-bit LAMB method preserves convergence and fine-tuning results. This refines the optimizer claim by showing outcomes depend on the compression strategy; the paper does not test the general adaptive-optimizer comparison in V4.
record.gate_note: Results on BERT-Large pre-training and downstream fine-tuning compare LAMB, 1-bit LAMB, and an experimental frozen-state compression method. The paper also measures optimizer scaling coefficients and variance over training. Cited findings from prior work and communication/runtime results alone are not rows for the claim.
record.test_reason: The study uses large-batch optimization to develop communication compression and evaluates its own optimizer variants. It does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD as V4 requires, or compare small and large batches under matched epoch budgets as V5 requires. Its compression ablations do not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that 1-bit LAMB preserves LAMB's sample-wise convergence and downstream fine-tuning accuracy while reducing communication and runtime. Freezing both variance and scaling coefficients degrades convergence and downstream scores.
record.recipe_differences: Compared with ordinary optimizer generalization comparisons, this study evaluates communication-compressed LAMB variants for BERT pre-training. 1-bit LAMB uses a LAMB warmup followed by error-compensated compressed momentum and adaptive layerwise scaling; the experimental basic 1-bit variant freezes variance and scaling coefficients. It does not report a train-test generalization gap.
record.method_sensitivity: The frozen-state compression strategy changes convergence and fine-tuning outcomes; 1-bit LAMB's revised adaptive layerwise scaling preserves them. Sequence length and batch size differ across reported evaluations.

fits_no_version.finding: At batch size 16K, 1-bit Adam has validation loss 1.504 versus LAMB's 1.362 and average SQuAD F1 89.225 versus 90.716.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At large batch size, LAMB can outperform compressed Adam under the tested BERT training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Basic frozen-state compression raises validation loss from 1.451 to 1.494 and lowers GLUE average from 83.9 to 82.1. Proposed 1-bit LAMB achieves validation loss 1.443 and GLUE average 83.9, with matching sample-wise convergence reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserving LAMB's convergence and downstream performance under communication compression depends on the compression and layerwise scaling strategy.

fits_no_version.finding: Layerwise scaling coefficients plateau at different times and levels, while many second-moment norms continue decreasing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LAMB's layerwise optimizer-state dynamics motivate adaptive scaling during compressed training.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on High Performance Computing, 2021
record.problems: No direct train-versus-test error or generalization-gap measure is reported. The optimizer comparison relevant to this catalog is limited to LAMB, 1-bit Adam and compressed LAMB variants, rather than the adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons in V4. Table 2 and Table 3 report 32-run summaries without error bars; Figure 2's curves are not numerically tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Communication profiling, compression volume, throughput, runtime, and NCCL-versus-MPI backend comparisons do not measure the claim’s generalization behavior and are not rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy in the same architectures and training recipes.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.

Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and controlled recipe adaptations. Tables 1 and 2 use different training schedules and sample budgets; batch-size sweeps report throughput.
Held-out effects of adding or removing dropout; dropout is configured but not experimentally varied.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not because the reported method comparisons are unreadable. Absence of a train-test gap alone would not exclude V4; the decisive omission is its adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
The paper does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD on held-out performance under the conditions in V4; it compares LAMB and compressed variants.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.

rows.subject: BERT-Large pre-training with LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Vanilla LAMB pre-training; reference for experimental frozen-state compression and 1-bit LAMB.
rows.measure: BERT validation loss; SQuAD 1.1 average/max dev set F1 over 32 runs
rows.value: validation loss 1.451; SQuAD Avg. F1 90.265; SQuAD Max F1 90.555
rows.note: Baseline row for the compressed variants; these measurements do not by themselves compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
rows.check: LAMB reference performance does not establish any listed effect; no SGD comparator or controlled batch-size comparison.

rows.subject: BERT-Large pre-training with LAMB + basic 1-bit
rows.operation_detail: Compression stage freezes both LAMB variance and scaling coefficient and communicates using 1-bit compressed momentum.
rows.measure: BERT validation loss; SQuAD 1.1 average/max dev set F1 over 32 runs
rows.baseline: LAMB: validation loss 1.451; SQuAD Avg. F1 90.265; SQuAD Max F1 90.555
rows.value: validation loss 1.494; SQuAD Avg. F1 90.069; SQuAD Max F1 90.409
rows.note: Authors say freezing both terms affects convergence speed and leads to lower SQuAD and GLUE scores.
rows.check: Measures the cost of freezing optimizer states during compression, not V4. Compression is applied only during sequence-length 128 training; sequence-length 512 uses vanilla LAMB.

rows.subject: BERT-Large pre-training with 1-bit LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Two-stage 1-bit LAMB: LAMB warmup followed by compressed momentum with adaptive layerwise scaling.
rows.measure: BERT validation loss; SQuAD 1.1 average/max dev set F1 over 32 runs
rows.baseline: LAMB: validation loss 1.451; SQuAD Avg. F1 90.265; SQuAD Max F1 90.555
rows.value: validation loss 1.443; SQuAD Avg. F1 90.524; SQuAD Max F1 90.788
rows.note: Authors report same convergence speed as vanilla LAMB for the proposed method.
rows.check: The proposed compression method's performance against LAMB is a method evaluation, not evidence for V4.

rows.subject: BERT-Large pre-training with LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Train with vanilla LAMB; comparator for 1-bit Adam under the same experiment.
rows.measure: BERT validation loss; SQuAD average/max dev set F1
rows.value: validation loss 1.362; SQuAD Avg. F1 90.716; SQuAD Max F1 91.119
rows.uncertainty: 32 runs for SQuAD scores; no error bar stated
rows.note: The first two rows of Table 1 are attributed to the original LAMB work; this row is the authors’ own LAMB experiment.
rows.check: LAMB reference performance does not test V4. Appendix A.1 specifies sequence lengths 128/512 and 28125/3125 steps.

rows.subject: BERT-Large pre-training with 1-bit Adam
rows.operation_detail: Train with 1-bit Adam and fine-tune the resulting model on SQuAD 1.1.
rows.measure: BERT validation loss; SQuAD average/max dev set F1
rows.baseline: LAMB: validation loss 1.362; SQuAD Avg. F1 90.716; SQuAD Max F1 91.119
rows.value: validation loss 1.504; SQuAD Avg. F1 89.225; SQuAD Max F1 89.494
rows.uncertainty: 32 runs for SQuAD scores; no error bar stated
rows.note: Authors describe 1-bit Adam as having slower convergence speed than LAMB at this larger batch size.
rows.check: Compares two adaptive optimizer recipes at batch size 16K; neither is an SGD baseline. The subject is BERT-Large, specified as 340M parameters in Section 6.

rows.subject: BERT-Large pre-training with LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Uncompressed LAMB pre-training; reference for 1-bit LAMB’s sample-wise training-loss curve.
rows.measure: Training loss as a function of samples
rows.note: Figure is described as showing the convergence results; text says 1-bit LAMB provides the same convergence speed as LAMB.
rows.check: Training-loss convergence alone does not measure held-out optimizer differences; this is a reference curve for the proposed method.

rows.subject: BERT-Large pre-training with 1-bit LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Two-stage 1-bit LAMB pre-training compared with uncompressed LAMB.
rows.measure: Training loss as a function of samples
rows.note: Text states 1-bit LAMB provides the same sample-wise convergence speed as LAMB for both sequence lengths.
rows.check: Matching LAMB's training-loss curve evaluates compression performance, not any listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: BERT-Large models pre-trained with LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune LAMB-pretrained models on each GLUE task.

conditions.value: MNLI-(m/mm), QQP, QNLI, SST-2, CoLA, STS-B, MRPC, RTE

rows.measure: GLUE development-set task scores and average
rows.value: MNLI 85.4/85.5; QQP 91.4; QNLI 91.9; SST-2 92.8; CoLA 60.9; STS-B 90.1; MRPC 86.9; RTE 70.4; Average 83.9
rows.uncertainty: median over 32 runs; no error bars stated
rows.note: GLUE fine-tuning uses Adam; this row is not a comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.
rows.check: Downstream reference scores compare pre-training compression recipes; all use Adam for fine-tuning.

rows.subject: BERT-Large models pre-trained with LAMB + basic 1-bit

rows.subject: BERT-Large pre-training with LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Measure layer-specific LAMB scaling coefficients during training.

conditions.value: different layers in first BertLayer; other layers said to have similar patterns

rows.note: Text reports coefficients keep increasing until plateaus and some become stable early; plateaus differ by layer. This measures an optimizer property, not a train-test generalization gap.
rows.check: Optimizer scaling coefficients are mechanism diagnostics, not a measure of any listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: BERT-Large pre-training with LAMB
rows.operation_detail: Measure layer-specific variance norms during training.

conditions.value: different layers in first BertLayer; other layers said to have similar patterns

rows.note: Text reports many layers’ variance norms continually decrease during training, up to two orders of magnitude. This is not a train-test generalization-gap measure.
rows.check: Optimizer second-moment norms are mechanism diagnostics, not magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization gaps.
